text: A natural transformation η between functors F, G: 𝒞 → 𝒟 consists of:
choices: a morphism η_A: F(A) → G(A) for each object A, such that G(f) ∘ η_A = η_B ∘ F(f) for every f: A → B
a morphism η_f for each morphism f of 𝒞
a single morphism F → G in the category 𝒞
an isomorphism F(A) ≅ G(A) for each object A, with no further condition
explanation: The components η_A must make every naturality square commute — that is what rules out arbitrary, choice-dependent maps. The double-dual embedding V → V** is natural; a family of isomorphisms V ≅ V* chosen basis-by-basis is not.
